newsitem.title: USA: Intel, other chipmakers rise on analyst comments.
newsitem.headline: Intel, other chipmakers rise on analyst comments.

text.p: The stock of microprocessor giant Intel Corp. and other computer companies surged Friday after Wall Street analysts issued bullish forecasts.

The technology-heavy Nasdaq Composite Index rose 20.58 to 1,301.28 at midday Friday, the first time the index has stood above 1,300 since Dec. 20. Intel rose $5.25 to $135.625 in afternoon trading on the Nasdaq market.

"We continue to see upside earnings surprise potential for the major U.S. semiconductor producers and recommend purchase of selected equities," including Intel, Merrill Lynch and Co. Inc. analyst Thomas Kurlak said in a report.

Santa Clara, Calif.-based Intel, the leading maker of the microprocessors that are the heart of personal computers, was also boosted by Salomon Brothers analyst Erika Klauer, who raised her rating for the stock to strong buy from hold.
"Intel got the major push, but that trickled over to everyone else," one trader said.

International Business Machines Corp. jumped $4.50 to $157.625 and Compaq Computer Corp. climbed $2.125 to $74.50 in afternoon trading on the New York Stock Exchange. Microsoft Corp. rose $1.50 to $83.125.
Friday's optimism followed a weak showing for technology stocks Thursday. Techs slid after computer retailer CompUSA Inc. posted disappointing December same-store sales.
"The technology sector is very sensitive -- susceptible to these mood swings," said Kenneth Ducey, director of trading at BT Brokerage, a subsidiary of Bankers Trust.

"Two days of trading into the new year, we're seeing erratic market swings. Investors have to get used to these types of mood changes -- it should continue like this for the rest of the year," Ducey said.
Kurlak predicted a quick recovery in the industry and forecast sales growth of 20 percent in 1997 and 42 percent in about two years.

Some other technology gainers included network company Cisco Systems Inc., which rose $1.625 to $64.50 on Nasdaq, and chip and computer maker Micron Technology Inc., which gained $1 to $30.625 on the New York Stock Exchange. Sun Microsystems Inc. added $1.125 to $27.875 and Oracle Corp. rose $1.75 to $43.75.
